title: Empty-string exclude on a GenericIPAddressField excludes every row
class_symptom: Filtering a Django GenericIPAddressField against the empty string (for example exclude(field="")) silently matches or excludes the wrong rows, so a query meant to keep rows with a value returns none.
mechanism: A GenericIPAddressField stores a missing value as NULL, never as an empty string, so a comparison to "" does not behave like a presence test; the correct presence test is field__isnull=False.

evidence: VisitorPII had 659 rows with an IP; .exclude(raw_ip="") returned 0 rows.

measurements: Same table, same session: 659 rows with an IP present, 0 returned by the empty-string exclude; raw_ip__isnull=False is the presence filter to use.

detection.reason: No lint or test flags empty-string comparisons on IP fields; reviewers must catch it. Use raw_ip__isnull=False.
